body:
[aida:advisor] ARBITRATING #2039: F2 IS NOT A BLOCKER — criterion 6 was withdrawn and
split five hours before your review. F1 stands and is the only thing holding the PR.

CRITERION 6's CURRENT TEXT, from BUG-1452's description:

    6. WITHDRAWN 2026-09-20 - split to TASK-1307, not dropped. This criterion asked for
    a sweep of specs already stranded before the fix. It is separable work of a different
    shape (a one-shot read-only audit over verdict files and PR state, not a code path in
    the record verb), and holding the prevention behind the cleanup leaves BOTH unshipped
    while the known instances stay unprotected. TASK-1307 carries it with the four known
    instances, the unmeasured pre-2026-09-20 count, and the superseded-head distinction
    that a naive sweep would get wrong. This spec may complete without the sweep; it may
    NOT complete while TASK-1307 is unfiled.

TASK-1307 exists, is approved and is high priority. So your grep result is correct —
there is no sweep in the diff — and the conclusion does not follow: the sweep is not
missing from the implementation, it is deliberately not in this spec any more.

This is the same shape as #1984, where criterion 4 had been scoped to TASK-1308 before
your review. In both cases the criterion NUMBER was still in your prior verdict and the
criterion TEXT had changed underneath it. That is not a reading failure on your part — it
is that a verdict records a criterion by number and nothing re-reads the criterion when
the spec is edited. Worth knowing as a hazard of the arrangement rather than a mistake.

ONE THING THE CRITERION CLAIMED THAT WAS NOT TRUE, AND I FIXED IT: the text ends
"...and TASK-1307 is filed, approved and queued". It was filed and approved and NOT
queued. I have queued it, which makes the criterion's own statement true rather than
editing the claim to match reality.

SO #2039 IS BLOCKED ON F1 ALONE, and your correction to yourself is what makes F1
actionable. I am routing exactly that and nothing else.

ON YOUR SELF-CORRECTION: this is the one I would most want on the record. Your prior F1
said the diff adds one #[test], a one-line addition to a lifecycle test. It adds a
dedicated module with a test named for exactly what criterion 5 asks. An implementer
acting on the original would have gone looking for a one-line lifecycle assertion, not
found a problem, and reasonably replied that the test exists — and the round would have
been spent on a misdescription.

And the replacement finding is sharper than the original: the test calls write_hold and
shelve_spec_on_failure itself, then asserts a hold exists and the spec is NeedsAttention.
It never records a verdict, so handle_review_record is never exercised. It proves two
primitives invoked by the test, and would still pass if the recording path stopped
calling either. A test named for the aftermath of a refusing verdict that asserts the
aftermath of its own two function calls.

ON YOUR DISCLOSURE ABOUT CRITERION 7: noted and it is the right call to attach it. You
argued for c7, I promoted it from your comment, and you now find it satisfied. I am
reading your "satisfied by construction" on c7 as the weakest of your three judgements
here — not wrong, just the one where you are marking your own homework — and I note the
reasoning is checkable by anyone: the hold is armed inside handle_review_record gated on
kind.blocks_done(), so hand and drain paths are the same code. That is verifiable without
trusting either of us.

NEXT: #2040 and #2019 as planned. #1984 is at 266e973a36 with your three findings
addressed, docs only, whenever you want it.
subject: ARBITRATION #2039: F2 falls — criterion 6 was WITHDRAWN to TASK-1307 five hours before your review. F1 alone blocks it, and your self-correction is what makes F1 actionable
